summary.headline: Ahead of target on orders and revenue this week, but YTD revenue is still behind target at 96.8%; the required run-rate now outpaces the recent 8-week pace.

points.what: Orders rose 5.1% WoW and 89.3% YoY to 1,030, a level outside the recent 8-week range.
points.so_what: That YoY pace is well above the 75% growth the targets assume, keeping the week ahead of the weekly target at 108.2%.

points.what: Revenue rose 1.3% WoW and 124.3% YoY to $78,682, also outside the 8-week range.
points.so_what: Revenue attainment came in at 107.5% of the weekly target, ahead alongside orders.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 96.8% of target.
points.so_what: The year remains behind target even with two ahead-of-target months in May and June.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% WoW while orders rose 5.1% WoW.
points.so_what: This week's revenue growth came from more orders rather than bigger baskets.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% WoW to $87.91.
points.so_what: This leaves revenue growth dependent on order volume rather than basket size, a risk given AOV's WoW decline.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 08 Jun rose to 9.7%, up 0.3pp WoW.
points.so_what: A rising return rate this week is a risk to watch for coming weeks.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run-rate of $71,736 is below the $84,542 needed for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At this pace, the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: Weekly orders were 108.2% of target and weekly revenue was 107.5% of target, both ahead.
points.so_what: The ahead-of-target week supported the quarter closing at 100.7% of target.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment finished the quarter at 100.7% of target.
points.so_what: The quarter closed ahead of target, offsetting the shortfall carried in year-to-date attainment.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 96.8% of target, with the required weekly run-rate of $84,542 versus the current 8-week run-rate of $71,736.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: North America was the top contributor to order growth, up 33.2% WoW and accounting for 130% of the week's net change in orders.
points.so_what: North America alone drove the week's increase in orders, more than offsetting declines elsewhere.

points.what: Search was the top traffic-source contributor, up 6.6% WoW and accounting for 90% of the week's net change in orders.
points.so_what: Order growth stayed concentrated in the largest channel rather than spreading across smaller sources.

points.what: APAC orders fell 2.0% WoW and EMEA fell 4.2% WoW, each subtracting from the week's total change.
points.so_what: These declines were more than offset by North America's growth, leaving overall orders still ahead of target.

points.what: AOV fell 5.2% WoW to $87.91, while still up 16.5% YoY.
points.so_what: With AOV falling, revenue's path to staying ahead of target depends more on order volume than basket size.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell to 13.1%, down 1.4pp WoW and down 1.4pp YoY, a notable improvement.
points.so_what: At $905 per point of cancellation rate, this improvement helped support the week's ahead-of-target revenue attainment.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 08 Jun rose to 9.7%, up 0.3pp WoW though down 0.6pp YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW increase is a risk to watch even as the year-on-year trend remains favorable.

points.what: New signups rose 1.2% WoW and 3.8% YoY to 244, far below orders' 89.3% YoY growth.
points.so_what: Order growth is outpacing new customer signups by a wide margin on a year-on-year basis.
